title.en: Clustering: k-means, hierarchical, and how to judge a clustering
title.zh: 聚类：k-means、层次聚类，以及怎么评价聚类

description.en: What clustering is for, k-means as coordinate descent on WCSS, agglomerative clustering with single, complete and average linkage by hand, and the WCSS, BCSS and Calinski-Harabasz measures.
description.zh: 聚类是做什么的，k-means 作为对 WCSS 的坐标下降，用单链、全链、平均链手算层次聚类，以及 WCSS、BCSS 和 Calinski-Harabasz 指标。

name.en: Unsupervised learning and kinds of clustering
name.zh: 无监督学习与聚类的种类

name.en: k-means: algorithm, convergence, limits, choosing K

name.zh: 凝聚层次聚类与各种链接

name.en: Cluster evaluation: WCSS, BCSS, CH index

description.en: Choosing K by minimising WCSS (it always falls as K grows, down to 0 at K = N)
description.zh: 用最小化 WCSS 来选 K（K 越大它越小，K = N 时为 0）

description.en: Believing k-means always finds the best clustering
description.zh: 以为 k-means 一定能找到最好的聚类

description.en: Mixing up single (min) and complete (max) linkage
description.zh: 把单链（取最小）和全链（取最大）弄反

description.en: Reading the distance matrix entries as coordinates
description.zh: 把距离矩阵里的数当成坐标

description.en: Reading a low CH index as better (higher is better)
description.zh: 以为 CH 指数小的更好（越大越好）

title.en: Clustering: structure from data alone

text.en: Labelling is slow and costly (a person usually has to do it), so labelled data is scarce while unlabelled data is everywhere. **Unsupervised learning** works with instances $\mathbf{x}$ only, with no labels $y$. The deck lists four kinds of task:
text.zh: 打标签又慢又贵（通常要人来做），所以有标签的数据很少，没标签的数据到处都是。**无监督学习**（unsupervised learning）只有实例 $\mathbf{x}$，没有标签 $y$。课件列了四类任务：

rows.en: a few directions that keep the most information of many features
rows.zh: 用少数几个方向保留多个特征里最多的信息

rows.en: rare items that differ from the pattern
rows.zh: 和常规模式不同的罕见实例

rows.en: rules that predict one item in a transaction from others
rows.zh: 根据交易里的某些商品预测另一些商品出现的规则

text.en: This lesson is about **clustering**: put similar instances in the same group and dissimilar ones in different groups. Nobody tells us how many groups there are or what they mean; we learn the structure from the data alone, so every clustering carries assumptions about what kind of structure to expect. Unsupervised results are hard to judge: they make only as much sense as you can make out of them. That is why the last chapter is about how to evaluate a clustering.
text.zh: 这一课讲**聚类**（clustering）：相似的实例放进同一组，不相似的放进不同的组。没人告诉我们有几组、每组是什么意思；结构只能从数据里学出来，所以每种聚类都带着对“结构长什么样”的假设。无监督的结果很难评判：你能从中读出多少意义，它就只有多少意义。所以最后一章专讲怎样评价聚类。

text.en: The deck sorts clustering by five yes/no questions about the structure we expect:
text.zh: 课件用五个是非问题，按我们期望的结构给聚类分类：

rows.en: Can an item be in more than one cluster?
rows.zh: 一个实例能属于多个簇吗？

rows.en: Can an item be only partly in a cluster?
rows.zh: 实例能“部分”属于一个簇吗？
簇之间有嵌套（树）关系吗？
每个实例都要被聚类吗？

rows.en: Are cluster sizes, shapes and densities alike?
rows.zh: 簇的大小、形状、密度相近吗？

text.en: The two methods of this lesson, k-means and agglomerative clustering, are both **exclusive, deterministic and complete**. They differ on one axis: k-means is **partitioning**, agglomerative is **hierarchical**.
text.zh: 这一课的两个方法，k-means 和凝聚聚类，都是**互斥、确定性、完全**的。区别在一条轴上：k-means 是**划分**式，凝聚聚类是**层次**式。

prompt.en: A soft clustering gives a customer the memberships (0.7, 0.3). Which description fits?
prompt.zh: 软聚类给某个顾客的隶属度是 (0.7, 0.3)。哪个描述对？

label.en: Deterministic: the customer is in cluster 1 because 0.7 is larger
label.zh: 确定性：0.7 更大，所以属于簇 1

feedback.en: Deterministic (hard) clustering outputs a single cluster, not a membership vector; picking the larger one afterwards hardens a soft result.
feedback.zh: 确定性（硬）聚类只给出一个簇，而不是隶属度向量；事后取较大者，是把软结果硬化。

label.en: Probabilistic (soft): the customer is partly in each cluster
label.zh: 概率性（软）：顾客部分属于每个簇

label.en: Overlapping: the customer fully belongs to both clusters
label.zh: 重叠：顾客完全属于两个簇

feedback.en: Overlapping means in or out for each cluster, possibly both; 0.7 / 0.3 are degrees of membership, a different axis.
feedback.zh: 重叠指对每个簇是“在或不在”，可以同时在两个簇里；0.7 / 0.3 是隶属程度，是另一条轴。

explain.en: Soft clustering returns a degree of membership per cluster; k-means and agglomerative clustering never do.
explain.zh: 软聚类对每个簇给出一个隶属程度；k-means 和凝聚聚类都不会这样。

title.en: k-means: K centroids, assign, move, repeat
title.zh: k-means：K 个质心，分配、移动、重复

text.en: Idea: represent each cluster by its centre (its **centroid**, the mean of its points) and let every instance belong to the nearest centre. Centres and memberships depend on each other, so we alternate.
text.zh: 想法：用中心（**质心** centroid，即簇内点的均值）代表每个簇，让每个实例属于最近的中心。中心和归属互相依赖，所以交替求解。

items.en: Ask for $K$, the number of clusters, and pick $K$ points at random as the starting centroids (the seeds).
items.zh: 先指定 $K$（簇的个数），随机挑 $K$ 个点作为起始质心（种子）。

items.en: **Assign** each instance to the cluster with the nearest centroid.
items.zh: **分配**：每个实例归到质心最近的簇。

items.en: **Update**: recompute each centroid as the mean of the instances now in its cluster.
items.zh: **更新**：把每个质心重算为当前簇内实例的均值。

items.en: Repeat 2 and 3 until the centroids stop changing (or move less than a threshold, or very few points change cluster).
items.zh: 重复 2、3，直到质心不再变化（或变化小于阈值，或几乎没有点换簇）。

title.en: Scale first

body.en: k-means (like k-NN) is distance based, so features on large scales dominate. Normalise each attribute, for example into $[0,1]$, before clustering. And the mean must make sense: it is ill-defined for categorical attributes.
body.zh: k-means（和 k-NN 一样）基于距离，数值范围大的特征会主导结果。聚类前先把每个属性规范化，例如缩放到 $[0,1]$。另外均值必须有意义：它对类别型属性没有定义。

text.en: k-means is exclusive, complete and partitioning, and it aims at **compact, spherical** clusters. Strengths from the deck: simple, fast and scalable to large datasets, easy to interpret and visualise, widely applicable, and good when clusters are round and well separated.
text.zh: k-means 是互斥、完全、划分式的，目标是**紧凑的球形**簇。课件列的优点：简单，快，能扩展到大数据集，结果易解释、易可视化，适用面广，簇是圆形且分得开时效果好。

title.en: k-means by hand on six numbers

say.en: Start: K = 2, and the two seeds are instances 1 and 2, so $\mu = (1, 2)$. **Assign** every point to its nearest centroid.
say.zh: 开始：K = 2，两个种子取 1 和 2，即 $\mu = (1, 2)$。**分配**：每个点归到最近的质心。

say.en: **Update**: each centroid becomes the mean of its points. The WCSS (sum of squared distances to the own centroid) is 54.8.
say.zh: **更新**：每个质心变成自己那组点的均值。WCSS（每个点到自己质心的距离平方之和）是 54.8。

say.en: Round 2: centroids $(1, 6.8)$. Assign each point to the nearer one (4 is 3 from $\mu_1$ and 2.8 from $\mu_2$ in this round).
say.zh: 第 2 轮：质心 $(1, 6.8)$。每个点归到更近的一个（这一轮里 4 离 $\mu_1$ 是 3，离 $\mu_2$ 是 2.8）。

say.en: **Update**: each centroid becomes the mean of its points. The WCSS (sum of squared distances to the own centroid) is 26.5.
say.zh: **更新**：每个质心变成自己那组点的均值。WCSS（每个点到自己质心的距离平方之和）是 26.5。

say.en: Round 3: centroids $(1.5, 8)$. Assign each point to the nearer one (4 is 2.5 from $\mu_1$ and 4 from $\mu_2$ in this round).
say.zh: 第 3 轮：质心 $(1.5, 8)$。每个点归到更近的一个（这一轮里 4 离 $\mu_1$ 是 2.5，离 $\mu_2$ 是 4）。

say.en: **Update**: each centroid becomes the mean of its points. The WCSS (sum of squared distances to the own centroid) is 9.33.
say.zh: **更新**：每个质心变成自己那组点的均值。WCSS（每个点到自己质心的距离平方之和）是 9.33。

say.en: Round 4: centroids $(2.333, 9.333)$. Assign each point to the nearer one (4 is 1.667 from $\mu_1$ and 5.333 from $\mu_2$ in this round).
**Update**: each centroid becomes the mean of its points. The WCSS (sum of squared distances to the own centroid) is 9.33. The centroids did not move: stop.
say.zh: **更新**：每个质心变成自己那组点的均值。WCSS（每个点到自己质心的距离平方之和）是 9.33。质心没有动：停止。

intro.en: One-dimensional data: $x = 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 11$, with $K = 2$ and the seeds 1 and 2. The exam would ask you to run exactly this.
intro.zh: 一维数据：$x = 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 11$，$K = 2$，种子取 1 和 2。考试就会让你这样走一遍。

outro.en: **Result:** clusters {1, 2, 4} and {8, 9, 11}, centroids 2.333 and 9.333, WCSS 9.33. Look at the WCSS column: it went down every round and never up. The next chapter shows why.
outro.zh: **结果：** 簇 {1, 2, 4} 和 {8, 9, 11}，质心 2.333 和 9.333，WCSS 9.33。看每轮的 WCSS：一直在降，从不上升。下一章解释为什么。

title.en: What k-means cannot do

rows.en: the algorithm has no way to decide it (next page)
rows.zh: 算法本身没办法决定 K（下一页）

rows.en: different seeds can end in different, worse solutions: a local optimum
rows.zh: 种子不同可能收敛到不同的、更差的解：局部最优

rows.en: a mean is dragged by extreme points, so a centroid can be pulled off its cluster
rows.zh: 均值会被极端点拖走，质心可能偏离簇

rows.en: it assigns by distance to a centre, so boundaries between clusters are straight lines
rows.zh: 按到中心的距离分配，所以簇之间的边界是直线

rows.en: a big cluster has points far from its centre; some are closer to a small neighbour, so the boundary cuts the big one
rows.zh: 大簇里有些点离自己的中心很远，反而离小邻居更近，边界就把大簇切掉一块

rows.en: the same reason: assignment uses distance only, not how densely the points sit
rows.zh: 同一个原因：分配只看距离，不看点有多密

rows.en: no mean of colours or words

title.en: Choosing K: the elbow method

text.en: k-means needs $K$ in advance, and the data rarely says how many groups there are. The **elbow method**: run k-means for a range of $K$, compute a quality measure for each (the usual one is the WCSS, defined in the last chapter), plot it against $K$, and look for the point after which the drop slows down sharply.
text.zh: k-means 要事先给定 $K$，而数据很少直接告诉你有几组。**肘部法**（elbow method）：对一系列 $K$ 都跑一次 k-means，算出质量指标（常用 WCSS，最后一章定义），把它对 $K$ 画出来，找出之后下降明显变缓的那一点。

title.en: Why not simply pick the K with the lowest WCSS?
title.zh: 为什么不直接选 WCSS 最小的 K？

body.en: WCSS never goes up as $K$ grows, and at $K = N$ every point is its own cluster with WCSS $= 0$. So the minimum is always the useless answer; the shape of the curve is what carries information.
body.zh: $K$ 变大时 WCSS 只会下降不会上升，$K = N$ 时每个点自成一簇，WCSS $= 0$。所以最小值总是没用的答案，有信息的是曲线的形状。

text.en: The elbow is a judgement call and sometimes there is none. A score that weighs compactness against $K$, such as the Calinski-Harabasz index at the end of this lesson, gives a number to compare instead.
text.zh: 肘部要靠判断，有时根本没有明显的肘。把紧凑程度和 $K$ 一起权衡的指标，例如本课最后的 Calinski-Harabasz 指数，则给出一个可以比较的数。

title.en: Deeper: why the mean is the best centre of a group
title.zh: 深入：为什么均值是一组点的最佳中心

say.en: Take one cluster with points $x_1, \dots, x_n$ and ask: which centre $c$ makes the sum of squared distances smallest? Call that sum $f(c)$.
say.zh: 取一个簇，里面有点 $x_1, \dots, x_n$。问：中心 $c$ 取多少，平方距离之和最小？把这个和记作 $f(c)$。

say.en: Differentiate with respect to $c$. Each term $(x_i - c)^2$ has derivative $-2(x_i - c)$ (chain rule).
say.zh: 对 $c$ 求导。每一项 $(x_i - c)^2$ 的导数是 $-2(x_i - c)$（链式法则）。

say.en: At a minimum the derivative is 0. Divide by $-2$ and split the sum: $\sum_i c = n c$ because $c$ does not depend on $i$.
say.zh: 最小值处导数为 0。两边除以 $-2$ 再拆开求和：$c$ 与 $i$ 无关，所以 $\sum_i c = n c$。

say.en: Solve for $c$: the best centre is the **mean**.
say.zh: 解出 $c$：最佳中心就是**均值**。

say.en: The second derivative is positive, so this stationary point is a minimum (and the only one: $f$ is a parabola).
say.zh: 二阶导数为正，所以这个驻点是最小值（也是唯一的：$f$ 是一条抛物线）。

say.en: Check with three points 2, 4, 9. The mean is 5.
say.zh: 用三个点 2, 4, 9 检验。均值是 5。

say.en: The sum of squares at the mean is 26; at another centre, say 4, it is 29, larger, as promised.
say.zh: 在均值处平方和是 26；在别的中心，比如 4，是 29，更大，正如推出的。

intro.en: k-means moves each centroid to the mean of its cluster. That is not a convention: it is the answer to a minimisation, derived here.
intro.zh: k-means 把每个质心移到簇的均值处。这不是约定，而是一个最小化问题的答案，现在把它推出来。

outro.en: So the update step is exactly *the best centres for the current groups*. The same algebra gives $\sum_i (x_i - c)^2 = \sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2 + n(\bar{x} - c)^2$, so any other $c$ pays an extra $n(\bar x - c)^2$.
outro.zh: 所以更新这一步恰好是“对当前分组的最佳中心”。同样的代数还给出 $\sum_i (x_i - c)^2 = \sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2 + n(\bar{x} - c)^2$，任何别的 $c$ 都要多付 $n(\bar x - c)^2$。

prompt.en: Evaluate the mean of the points 2, 4 and 9.
prompt.zh: 算出 2、4、9 这三个点的均值。

title.en: Deeper: k-means as coordinate descent on WCSS
title.zh: 深入：k-means 是对 WCSS 的坐标下降

say.en: What k-means secretly minimises. $a_i \in \{1..K\}$ is the cluster of instance $i$, $\mu_j$ is the centre of cluster $j$. $J$ is the WCSS: every point's squared distance to the centre of its own cluster.
say.zh: k-means 暗中在最小化的东西。$a_i \in \{1..K\}$ 是实例 $i$ 所在的簇，$\mu_j$ 是簇 $j$ 的中心。$J$ 就是 WCSS：每个点到自己簇中心的距离平方之和。

say.en: **Assignment step** = minimise $J$ over $a$ with $\mu$ fixed. $J$ is a sum of $N$ terms, term $i$ depends only on $a_i$, so each point can choose on its own: its nearest centre.
say.zh: **分配步** = 固定 $\mu$，对 $a$ 最小化 $J$。$J$ 是 $N$ 项之和，第 $i$ 项只依赖 $a_i$，所以每个点可以各自挑选：最近的那个中心。

say.en: Each point either keeps its cluster or moves to one that is at least as near, so no term gets bigger.
say.zh: 每个点要么留在原簇，要么换到不比原来远的簇，所以没有哪一项变大。

say.en: **Update step** = minimise $J$ over $\mu$ with $a$ fixed. $J$ splits into one sum per cluster, and in each the best centre is the mean (previous page, applied per coordinate).
say.zh: **更新步** = 固定 $a$，对 $\mu$ 最小化 $J$。$J$ 拆成每个簇一个和，每个簇里最佳中心都是均值（上一页的结论，逐个坐标成立）。

say.en: The mean is the minimiser, so replacing any centre by it cannot make its cluster's sum bigger.
say.zh: 均值是最小值点，把中心换成它，该簇的平方和不可能变大。

say.en: Each round is an assignment step then an update step, each never increasing $J$. So $J$ is a non-increasing sequence bounded below by 0.
say.zh: 每一轮是一次分配加一次更新，两步都不增加 $J$。所以 $J$ 是一个不增、且下界为 0 的序列。

say.en: There are only finitely many ways to split $N$ points into $K$ groups: the set $\mathcal{P}$ of partitions has at most $K^N$ members. After an update, the centres are determined by the partition, and $J$ is a function of the partition.
say.zh: 把 $N$ 个点分成 $K$ 组的方式只有有限种。更新之后，中心由分组决定，$J$ 是分组的函数。

say.en: With ties broken consistently, a round (partition $\mathcal{P}_t \to \mathcal{P}_{t+1}$) either lowers $J$ strictly or leaves the partition unchanged ($\lor$ means
say.zh: 平局按固定规则处理时，每一轮要么让 $J$ 严格下降（得到新的分组），要么什么都不变。若分组重复，$J$ 必须保持不变，也就是已经停了，所以算法在有限轮内一定停下。

intro.en: Why does k-means stop, and does it stop at the best clustering? Both answers come from reading the two steps as *minimise over one block of unknowns while the other is held fixed*: coordinate descent.
intro.zh: k-means 为什么会停，停下来的是不是最好的聚类？两个答案都来自一个读法：把两步看成“固定一组未知量，对另一组求最小”，也就是坐标下降。

outro.en: **It converges, but only to a fixed point:** a pair $(a, \mu)$ that neither step can improve. That is a *local* minimum of $J$ (a minimum along each block), not necessarily the global one, because $J$ is not convex in $(a, \mu)$ together.
outro.zh: **它一定收敛，但只收敛到一个不动点**：一对 $(a, \mu)$，两步都改进不了。这是 $J$ 的*局部*最小值（沿每一块坐标是最小），不一定是全局最小，因为 $J$ 对 $(a, \mu)$ 整体并不是凸的。

title.en: Deeper: a local optimum you can compute
title.zh: 深入：一个能算出来的局部最优

text.en: Take $x = 0, 1, 5, 6, 11, 12$ with $K = 3$. The obvious clusters are the three adjacent pairs. Run k-means from two different seed sets:
text.zh: 取 $x = 0, 1, 5, 6, 11, 12$，$K = 3$。显然的簇是三对相邻的点。从两组不同的种子出发跑 k-means：

text.en: The second run is a true fixed point: the centroids are 0, 1 and 8.5; every point is nearest to its own centroid (6 is 2.5 from 8.5 and 5 from 1), so nothing moves. Yet its WCSS is 37 against 1.5: k-means gives no guarantee about which one you get.
text.zh: 第二次是真正的不动点：质心是 0、1 和 8.5；每个点离自己的质心最近（6 离 8.5 是 2.5，离 1 是 5），所以谁也不动。可它的 WCSS 是 37，另一个只有 1.5：k-means 不保证你得到哪一个。

text.en: In practice: run it several times from different random seeds and keep the lowest WCSS, or choose seeds that are far apart (the idea of k-means++, a textbook refinement, not in the deck).
text.zh: 实际做法：用不同随机种子多跑几次，留下 WCSS 最小的那个；或者让种子彼此相距较远（k-means++ 的思路，是教材里的改进，课件没讲）。

prompt.en: Which statement about k-means is true?
prompt.zh: 关于 k-means，哪句话是对的？

label.en: It always finds the clustering with the lowest WCSS
label.zh: 它总能找到 WCSS 最低的聚类

feedback.en: It only finds a local optimum: the example above stops at WCSS 37 although 1.5 is possible.
feedback.zh: 它只能找到局部最优：上面的例子停在 WCSS 37，而 1.5 是可能的。

label.en: It might loop forever because the centroids can keep moving
label.zh: 质心可能一直动，所以可能永远不停

feedback.en: It always terminates: J falls or the partition stays, and there are finitely many partitions.
feedback.zh: 它一定会停：J 下降或分组不变，而分组只有有限种。

label.en: It always stops, but possibly at a local optimum that depends on the seeds
label.zh: 它一定会停，但可能停在取决于种子的局部最优

explain.en: Termination is guaranteed by the coordinate-descent argument; optimality is not.
explain.zh: 终止由坐标下降的论证保证；最优性没有保证。

title.en: Hierarchical clustering: a tree of merges

text.en: Instead of one flat split, hierarchical clustering produces **nested** clusters, recorded as a tree called a **dendrogram**: the height of each bar is the distance at which two clusters were merged. Cutting the tree horizontally gives any number of clusters you like.
text.zh: 层次聚类不是一刀平面切分，而是产生**嵌套**的簇，记成一棵树，叫**树状图**（dendrogram）：每根横线的高度就是两个簇被合并时的距离。在某个高度横着切一刀，就得到相应个数的簇。

rows.en: every instance is its own cluster

rows.zh: 只剩一个簇（或剩 K 个）
每个点一簇（或得到 K 个簇）

text.en: Both use a distance (proximity) matrix between instances. This lesson works agglomerative clustering fully; divisive is its mirror image and is covered only at this level in the deck. The algorithm: make each point a cluster, compute the distance matrix, then repeat *merge the two closest clusters, update the matrix* until one cluster remains.
text.zh: 两者都用实例之间的距离（相似度）矩阵。这一课把凝聚聚类算完整；分裂聚类是它的镜像，课件也只讲到这个程度。算法：每个点当一个簇，算距离矩阵，然后重复“合并最近的两个簇、更新矩阵”，直到只剩一个簇。

text.en: The only open question is the distance between two *clusters*. The deck lists four answers:
text.zh: 唯一没定的是两个*簇*之间的距离。课件给了四种答案：

rows.en: closest pair: $\min_{a \in A, b \in B} d(a, b)$
rows.zh: 最近的一对：$\min_{a \in A, b \in B} d(a, b)$

rows.en: farthest pair: $\max_{a \in A, b \in B} d(a, b)$
rows.zh: 最远的一对：$\max_{a \in A, b \in B} d(a, b)$

rows.en: mean of all pairs: $\frac{1}{|A||B|}\sum_{a, b} d(a, b)$
rows.zh: 所有配对的平均：$\frac{1}{|A||B|}\sum_{a, b} d(a, b)$

title.en: Single linkage on the deck's 5-instance matrix
title.zh: 在课件的 5 实例矩阵上做单链

say.en: The matrix of distances between the 5 instances (the numbers are distances, not coordinates). The smallest off-diagonal entry is 5, between instances 1 and 4. This first step is the same for every linkage: merge them, at height 5.
say.zh: 5 个实例两两之间的距离矩阵（里面是距离，不是坐标）。除对角线外最小的数是 5，在实例 1 和 4 之间。这一步对所有链接方式都一样：把它们合并，高度为 5。

say.en: Single linkage: the distance between two clusters is the **smallest** distance between a member of one and a member of the other. So each new entry is the min of the two old entries.
say.zh: 单链（single linkage）：两个簇之间的距离取两簇成员之间**最小**的那个距离。所以每个新数就是两个旧数里较小的。

say.en: Smallest entry now: 10, between {1,4} and {5}. Merge them at height 10, and recompute that cluster's row with the same rule.
say.zh: 现在最小的数是 10，在 {1,4} 和 {5} 之间。在高度 10 把它们合并，再用同一条规则重算这个簇的那一行。

say.en: Smallest entry now: 15, between {1,4,5} and {2}. Merge them at height 15, and recompute that cluster's row with the same rule.
say.zh: 现在最小的数是 15，在 {1,4,5} 和 {2} 之间。在高度 15 把它们合并，再用同一条规则重算这个簇的那一行。

say.en: Two clusters left, {1,2,4,5} and {3}, at distance 30. The last merge puts everything into one cluster at height 30.
say.zh: 只剩两个簇 {1,2,4,5} 和 {3}，距离 30。最后一次合并把所有实例并成一个簇，高度 30。

say.en: The merge sequence, in order. The heights are 5, 10, 15, 30; those are the heights of the dendrogram's horizontal bars.
say.zh: 合并顺序如上。各次合并的高度依次为 5, 10, 15, 30，它们就是树状图（dendrogram）里横线的高度。

intro.en: The cells of the matrix are the distances between instances, *not* coordinates. Five instances, so four merges.
intro.zh: 矩阵里的数是实例之间的距离，*不是*坐标。五个实例，所以合并四次。

outro.en: Single linkage keeps the **minimum** each time, so clusters grow by their closest pair: 5, 10, 15, 30.
outro.zh: 单链每次都取**最小**，簇靠最近的一对往外长：5、10、15、30。

title.en: Complete linkage on the same matrix

say.en: The matrix of distances between the 5 instances (the numbers are distances, not coordinates). The smallest off-diagonal entry is 5, between instances 1 and 4. This first step is the same for every linkage: merge them, at height 5.
say.zh: 5 个实例两两之间的距离矩阵（里面是距离，不是坐标）。除对角线外最小的数是 5，在实例 1 和 4 之间。这一步对所有链接方式都一样：把它们合并，高度为 5。

say.en: Complete linkage: the distance between two clusters is the **largest** distance between a member of one and a member of the other. Each new entry is the max of the two old entries.
say.zh: 全链（complete linkage）：两个簇之间的距离取两簇成员之间**最大**的那个距离。每个新数就是两个旧数里较大的。

say.en: Smallest entry now: 20, between {1,4} and {2}. Merge them at height 20, and recompute that cluster's row with the same rule.
say.zh: 现在最小的数是 20，在 {1,4} 和 {2} 之间。在高度 20 把它们合并，再用同一条规则重算这个簇的那一行。

say.en: Smallest entry now: 40, between {3} and {5}. Merge them at height 40, and recompute that cluster's row with the same rule.
say.zh: 现在最小的数是 40，在 {3} 和 {5} 之间。在高度 40 把它们合并，再用同一条规则重算这个簇的那一行。

say.en: Two clusters left, {1,2,4} and {3,5}, at distance 50. The last merge puts everything into one cluster at height 50.
say.zh: 只剩两个簇 {1,2,4} 和 {3,5}，距离 50。最后一次合并把所有实例并成一个簇，高度 50。

say.en: The merge sequence, in order. The heights are 5, 20, 40, 50; those are the heights of the dendrogram's horizontal bars.
say.zh: 合并顺序如上。各次合并的高度依次为 5, 20, 40, 50，它们就是树状图（dendrogram）里横线的高度。

intro.en: Same matrix, same first merge. Only the update rule changes: keep the **maximum**.
intro.zh: 同一个矩阵，第一次合并也一样。只有更新规则变了：取**最大**。

outro.en: The two linkages disagree after step 1: single ends with 3 joined last at 30, complete pairs (3, 5) at 40 and joins everything at 50.
outro.zh: 第 1 步之后两种链接就分道扬镳：单链最后在 30 把 3 接上，全链先在 40 把 (3, 5) 配成一对，最后在 50 合并所有。

title.en: Average linkage on the same matrix
title.zh: 同一个矩阵上做平均链

say.en: The matrix of distances between the 5 instances (the numbers are distances, not coordinates). The smallest off-diagonal entry is 5, between instances 1 and 4. This first step is the same for every linkage: merge them, at height 5.
say.zh: 5 个实例两两之间的距离矩阵（里面是距离，不是坐标）。除对角线外最小的数是 5，在实例 1 和 4 之间。这一步对所有链接方式都一样：把它们合并，高度为 5。

say.en: Average linkage: the distance between two clusters is the **mean** of all pairwise distances between their members. Here every pair involves one member of {1,4}, so each new entry is the mean of two old entries (in general, weight by cluster sizes).
say.zh: 平均链（average linkage）：两个簇之间的距离取两簇成员所有配对距离的**平均**。这里每对里都有 {1,4} 的一个成员，所以新数是两个旧数的平均（一般情况下要按簇的大小加权）。

say.en: Smallest entry now: 17.5, between {1,4} and {2}. Merge them at height 17.5, and recompute that cluster's row with the same rule.
say.zh: 现在最小的数是 17.5，在 {1,4} 和 {2} 之间。在高度 17.5 把它们合并，再用同一条规则重算这个簇的那一行。

say.en: Smallest entry now: 26.67, between {1,2,4} and {5}. Merge them at height 26.67, and recompute that cluster's row with the same rule.
say.zh: 现在最小的数是 26.67，在 {1,2,4} 和 {5} 之间。在高度 26.67 把它们合并，再用同一条规则重算这个簇的那一行。

say.en: Two clusters left, {1,2,4,5} and {3}, at distance 38.75. The last merge puts everything into one cluster at height 38.75.
say.zh: 只剩两个簇 {1,2,4,5} 和 {3}，距离 38.75。最后一次合并把所有实例并成一个簇，高度 38.75。

say.en: The merge sequence, in order. The heights are 5, 17.5, 26.67, 38.75; those are the heights of the dendrogram's horizontal bars.
say.zh: 合并顺序如上。各次合并的高度依次为 5, 17.5, 26.67, 38.75，它们就是树状图（dendrogram）里横线的高度。

intro.en: Average linkage sits between the two extremes: it uses the mean of all pair distances.
intro.zh: 平均链介于两个极端之间：用所有配对距离的平均。

outro.en: Same first merge again; heights 5, 17.5, 26.67, 38.75. Centroid linkage (distance between centroids) needs coordinates rather than just this matrix; the deck shows only that its tree can violate the hierarchy (a later merge can be lower than an earlier one, an *inversion*) and that it is sensitive to outliers, like k-means.
outro.zh: 第一次合并还是一样；高度 5、17.5、26.67、38.75。质心链（质心之间的距离）需要坐标，光有这个矩阵不够；课件只指出：它的树可能违反层次结构（后一次合并的高度可以比前一次低，叫*倒挂*），并且像 k-means 一样对离群点敏感。

caption.en: Heights are the merge distances. Cut at a height to read off the clusters.
caption.zh: 高度是合并距离。在某个高度切开，就读出相应的簇。

text.en: To read off K = 2 clusters, cut below the last merge. Single: {1,4,5,2} and {3}. Complete: {1,4,2} and {3,5}. Average: {1,4,2,5} and {3}. Different linkages, different answers on the same data: the linkage is a modelling choice, like the distance.
text.zh: 要读出 K = 2 个簇，就在最后一次合并之下切。单链：{1,4,5,2} 和 {3}。全链：{1,4,2} 和 {3,5}。平均链：{1,4,2,5} 和 {3}。同样的数据、不同的链接，答案不同：链接是一个建模选择，和距离的选择一样。

prompt.en: In the complete-linkage run, why is 5 not merged with {1,4,2} at height 25 (its distance to 2)?
prompt.zh: 全链里，为什么 5 没有在高度 25（它到 2 的距离）处并进 {1,4,2}？

label.en: Complete linkage measures the *farthest* pair: from 5 to {1,4,2} that is 45
label.zh: 全链看的是*最远*的一对：5 到 {1,4,2} 是 45

label.en: Because 25 is bigger than 20
label.zh: 因为 25 比 20 大

feedback.en: Merges are chosen by the smallest cluster distance in the current matrix; the cluster distance here is not 25.
feedback.zh: 合并选的是当前矩阵里最小的簇间距离；这里簇间距离不是 25。

label.en: Because complete linkage only merges instances, never clusters
label.zh: 因为全链只合并实例，不合并簇

feedback.en: It merges clusters like any agglomerative method.
feedback.zh: 它和其他凝聚方法一样合并簇。

explain.en: One far member keeps a cluster away under complete linkage.
explain.zh: 全链下，只要有一个成员离得远，整个簇就远。

title.en: Deeper: why single chains and complete stays compact
title.zh: 深入：单链为何会“串成一条”、全链为何偏紧凑

text.en: Single linkage asks only: is there *some* pair, one in each cluster, that is close? Then a thin strand of points between two groups is a chain of small steps, and each step merges at a small height. Complete linkage asks: are *all* pairs close? A cluster's distance to anything is at least the distance across its own spread, so clusters only merge while they stay compact.
text.zh: 单链只问：两个簇里是否*有一对*点离得近？那么两组之间一条稀疏的点链就是一连串小步，每一步都在很低的高度合并。全链问的是：*所有*配对是否都近？簇和任何东西的距离至少是它自身展开的跨度，所以簇只有在保持紧凑时才会合并。

rows.zh: 偏好紧凑、直径相近的簇，容易把大簇拆开

prompt.en: A few noisy points lie in a line between two clearly separate groups. Which linkage merges the two groups first?
prompt.zh: 两个明显分开的组之间有几个噪声点连成一线。哪种链接会最先把两组并到一起？

label.en: Complete linkage
label.zh: 全链

feedback.en: Complete linkage looks at the farthest pair, which stays large however many points lie in between.
feedback.zh: 全链看最远的一对，中间有多少点都不会让它变小。

label.en: Single linkage
label.zh: 单链

label.en: Both merge them at the same height
label.zh: 两者在同一高度合并

feedback.en: Single links through the strand at tiny steps; complete does not.
feedback.zh: 单链通过细链用很小的步子连上；全链不会。

explain.en: That is chaining: single linkage follows the shortest hops.
explain.zh: 这就是链式效应：单链顺着最短的跳跃走。

title.en: Hierarchical clustering against k-means
title.zh: 层次聚类和 k-means 的对比

rows.en: no: cut the dendrogram at any level
rows.zh: 不要：在任意高度切树状图

rows.en: no assumption on shape; depends on the linkage
rows.zh: 对形状没有假设；取决于链接方式

rows.en: none: no objective function is directly minimised, so no "relative" quality measure
rows.zh: 没有：不直接最小化任何目标函数，也就没有“相对”的质量度量

rows.en: points can move between clusters every round
a merge can never be undone: a point in the wrong cluster stays there
rows.zh: 合并后不能撤销：进错簇的点永远在里面

rows.en: needs the full distance matrix, so costly for large N
rows.zh: 需要完整距离矩阵，N 大时开销大（教材常识）

text.en: Hierarchical clustering can also give meaningful taxonomies (animal kingdom, phylogeny). Both families are sensitive to outliers in some way: k-means through its means, single linkage through chaining, centroid linkage like k-means.
text.zh: 层次聚类还能给出有意义的分类体系（动物界、系统发生树）。两类方法都在某种意义上怕离群点：k-means 通过均值，单链通过链式效应，质心链和 k-means 一样。

title.en: Evaluating a clustering: cohesion and separation
title.zh: 评价聚类：凝聚度与分离度

text.en: There are no true labels to compare with, so the measures ask what a good clustering looks like by itself. A good clustering has one or both of:
text.zh: 没有真实标签可对照，所以这些指标只问：一个好的聚类本身应该是什么样。好的聚类具备下面一条或两条：

items.en: **High cohesion** (compactness): instances in a cluster are close to each other. Measured by the **WCSS**, the within-cluster sum of squares. Lower is better.
items.zh: **高凝聚度**（紧凑）：簇内实例彼此接近。用 **WCSS**（簇内平方和）衡量，越小越好。

items.en: **High separation** (distinct clusters): different clusters are far apart. Measured by the **BCSS**, the between-cluster sum of squares. Higher is better.
items.zh: **高分离度**（簇间分得开）：不同的簇彼此远离。用 **BCSS**（簇间平方和）衡量，越大越好。

text.en: For each cluster $C_j$ with mean $\mu_j$, add up each member's squared distance to it, then add over clusters. This is the same $J$ k-means minimises.
text.zh: 对每个簇 $C_j$（均值 $\mu_j$），把每个成员到它的距离平方加起来，再对簇求和。这和 k-means 最小化的 $J$ 是同一个量。

text.en: Here $\mu$ is the mean of all the data and $n_j$ the size of cluster $j$: how far each cluster centre lies from the overall centre, counted once per member, so big clusters count more.
text.zh: 这里 $\mu$ 是全部数据的均值，$n_j$ 是簇 $j$ 的大小：每个簇的中心离总体中心多远，每个成员算一次，所以大簇权重更大。

text.en: The deck's summary lists unsupervised metrics (the cohesion and separation above) and supervised ones. The slides show only the former, so what follows is the textbook version of the rest, to be able to answer \"how else would you evaluate a clustering?\".
text.zh: 课件的小结列了无监督指标（上面的凝聚度和分离度）和有监督指标。幻灯片只展示了前者，下面是教材里其余部分的标准说法，用来回答“还有什么办法评价聚类”。

text.en: For one instance, let $a$ be its mean distance to the other members of its own cluster and $b$ its mean distance to the members of the nearest other cluster. The silhouette is $s = (b - a)/\max(a, b) \in [-1, 1]$: near 1 well placed, near 0 on a boundary, negative probably in the wrong cluster. The mean over all instances scores a clustering and can be compared across $K$.
text.zh: 对一个实例，设 $a$ 为它到本簇其他成员的平均距离，$b$ 为它到最近的其他簇成员的平均距离。轮廓系数 $s = (b - a)/\max(a, b) \in [-1, 1]$：接近 1 表示位置很好，接近 0 表示在边界上，负数说明可能分错了簇。对所有实例取平均，就能给一个聚类打分，并跨 $K$ 比较。

summary.en: When labels exist: purity and entropy (textbook)
summary.zh: 有标签时：纯度和熵（教材）

text.en: If true classes are known (not used for clustering), compare them with the clusters. **Purity**: for each cluster take the count of its most common class, sum these, divide by $N$. **Entropy**: for each cluster compute $-\sum_c p_{jc}\log_2 p_{jc}$ over the class proportions in it, and average weighted by cluster size; lower is purer. Purity is easy to read but is trivially 1 when every point is its own cluster, so it must be used with a fixed $K$.
text.zh: 如果知道真实类别（聚类时没用到），就拿它们和簇对比。**纯度**（purity）：对每个簇取其中最多的那个类的个数，求和后除以 $N$。**熵**：对每个簇，按其中各类的比例算 $-\sum_c p_{jc}\log_2 p_{jc}$，再按簇大小加权平均；越小越纯。纯度好读，但每个点自成一簇时它平凡地等于 1，所以只能在 $K$ 固定时用。

title.en: Deeper: WCSS and BCSS add up to a constant
title.zh: 深入：WCSS 与 BCSS 之和是常数

say.en: The **total** sum of squares: every point's squared distance to the overall mean $\mu$. It depends only on the data, not on any clustering.
say.zh: **总**平方和：每个点到总体均值 $\mu$ 的距离平方之和。它只取决于数据，与任何聚类无关。

say.en: For a point $i$ in cluster $j$, go through the cluster mean: first from the point to its cluster centre, then from there to the overall centre.
say.zh: 对簇 $j$ 里的点 $i$，经过簇均值走一步：先从点到簇中心，再从簇中心到总体中心。

say.en: Expand the square of a sum.
say.zh: 展开和的平方。

say.en: Summed over the points of one cluster, the cross term vanishes: the deviations from a cluster's own mean add to zero (that is what a mean is).
say.zh: 在同一簇的点上求和，交叉项消失：到自己簇均值的偏差加起来为零（均值的定义就是这样）。

say.en: What is left: the first term summed gives WCSS, and the second, which is the same for all $n_j$ members, gives $n_j\lVert \mu_j - \mu \rVert^2$, i.e. BCSS.
say.zh: 剩下的：第一项求和是 WCSS；第二项对 $n_j$ 个成员都一样，求和得 $n_j\lVert \mu_j - \mu \rVert^2$，也就是 BCSS。

say.en: Check on the deck's six points $0, 0.5, 1, 3, 4, 5$ (next page) with clusters $\{0,0.5,1\}$, $\{3,4,5\}$.

intro.en: Why are WCSS and BCSS two sides of one coin?
intro.zh: 为什么 WCSS 和 BCSS 像是一枚硬币的两面？

outro.en: The total is fixed, so for a given dataset **lowering WCSS and raising BCSS are the same move**. That is why k-means (which minimises WCSS) also pushes clusters apart, and why the CH index below can be written with either.
outro.zh: 总量固定，所以对同一份数据，**降低 WCSS 和提高 BCSS 是同一件事**。这就是 k-means（最小化 WCSS）同时也把簇推开的原因，也是下面 CH 指数用哪个都能写的原因。

title.en: Calinski-Harabasz: one number for the trade-off

text.en: WCSS alone always improves with more clusters. The **Calinski-Harabasz (CH) index**, also called the variance ratio criterion, uses both compactness and separation and charges for $K$:
text.zh: 光看 WCSS，簇越多总是越好。**Calinski-Harabasz（CH）指数**，也叫方差比准则，同时用紧凑度和分离度，并对 $K$ 收费：

items.en: $BCSS/WCSS$: how much of the spread is between clusters relative to within them. Bigger = better separated and more compact.
items.zh: $BCSS/WCSS$：簇间的离散程度相对簇内的比值。越大 = 分得越开、越紧凑。

items.en: $(N-K)/(K-1)$: divides each sum by its degrees of freedom (BCSS has $K - 1$ free centres, WCSS has $N - K$ free points), so a larger $K$ does not win just by cutting WCSS.
items.zh: $(N-K)/(K-1)$：把每个平方和除以自己的自由度（BCSS 有 $K-1$ 个自由的中心，WCSS 有 $N-K$ 个自由的点），所以 $K$ 大并不能只靠压低 WCSS 取胜。

items.en: **Higher CH = better-defined clusters.** Compare the same dataset under different clusterings or different $K$; the absolute value alone means little.
items.zh: **CH 越高 = 簇划分得越清晰。** 在同一份数据上比较不同聚类或不同 $K$；单个数值本身没多少意义。

title.en: The deck's example: A (K = 2) or B (K = 3)?

say.en: Six points on a line. Clustering A: $\{0, 0.5, 1\}$ and $\{3, 4, 5\}$. Clustering B: $\{0, 0.5\}$, $\{1, 3\}$ and $\{4, 5\}$.
The overall mean: the sum is 13.5, divided by 6.
say.zh: 总体均值：和是 13.5，除以 6。

say.en: Clustering A: the two cluster means.
say.zh: 聚类 A：两个簇的均值。

say.en: Squared distances to the own mean, cluster by cluster.
say.zh: 逐簇，每个点到自己簇均值的距离平方。

say.en: Each cluster has 3 members; each centre is 1.75 from the overall mean.
say.zh: 每个簇 3 个成员；每个簇中心离总体均值 1.75。

say.en: Plug in: $N = 6$, $K = 2$.
Clustering B: the three cluster means.
say.zh: 聚类 B：三个簇的均值。

say.en: The pair $\{1, 3\}$ alone costs 2: it is the loose cluster.
say.zh: 仅 $\{1, 3\}$ 这一簇就是 2：它是松散的那一个。

say.en: Each cluster has 2 members. The centres 0.25, 2 and 4.5 are 2, 0.25 and 2.25 away from the overall mean 2.25.
say.zh: 每个簇 2 个成员。三个中心 0.25、2、4.5 到总体均值 2.25 的距离分别是 2、0.25、2.25。

say.en: Plug in: $N = 6$, $K = 3$.

intro.en: Which clustering of the same six points is better, according to the CH index?
intro.zh: 同样六个点，按 CH 指数，哪种聚类更好？

outro.en: **A wins: 29.4 against 10.43.** A's clusters are both tighter (WCSS 2.5 against 2.625) and a little more separated, with fewer clusters to pay for.
outro.zh: **A 胜：29.4 对 10.43。** A 的簇更紧（WCSS 2.5 对 2.625），分得也略开一点，还少付一些 $K$ 的代价。

title.en: Compute a CH index

prompt.en: Same data as the previous question: $\{1, 3\}$ and $\{8, 10, 12\}$ ($N = 5$, $K = 2$). Compute the CH index. Round to 1 decimal place.

title.en: Choosing K

prompt.en: A student runs k-means for $K = 1, \dots, 10$ and reports $K = 10$ because it has the lowest WCSS. What is wrong?
prompt.zh: 一位同学对 $K = 1, \dots, 10$ 各跑一次 k-means，因为 $K = 10$ 的 WCSS 最低就选了它。问题在哪？

label.en: WCSS is only meaningful for K up to 5
label.zh: WCSS 只在 K 不超过 5 时有意义

label.en: WCSS can only fall as K grows (zero at K = N), so its minimum is uninformative; look for an elbow or use a score such as CH
label.zh: K 越大 WCSS 只会下降（K = N 时为零），所以最小值没有信息；应看肘部，或用 CH 之类的指标

label.en: k-means is not allowed to use K larger than the number of features
label.zh: k-means 的 K 不能超过特征数

feedback.en: K is limited by N, not by the number of features.
feedback.zh: K 受 N 限制，而不是受特征数限制。

explain.en: Selecting K needs a criterion that does not improve automatically with K.
explain.zh: 选 K 需要一个不会随 K 自动变好的标准。

title.en: Which linkage?

prompt.en: Data: two long, thin, curved groups, plus a few noise points scattered far away. Which linkage would you worry about, and why?
prompt.zh: 数据：两个细长弯曲的组，外加几个远处散落的噪声点。你会担心哪种链接，为什么？

label.en: Complete linkage tends to prefer compact, equal-diameter clusters and break long ones, so it will cut the thin groups
label.zh: 全链偏好紧凑、直径相近的簇，会把细长的组拆开

label.en: Single linkage, because it takes the farthest pair and noise is far away
label.zh: 单链，因为它取最远的一对而噪声很远

feedback.en: Single takes the *closest* pair; the farthest pair is complete linkage. (Single is sensitive to noise for another reason: strands of noise chain clusters.)
feedback.zh: 单链取的是*最近*的一对，最远的一对是全链。（单链怕噪声是另一个原因：噪声串成链会把簇接起来。）

label.en: Neither: hierarchical clustering ignores noise
label.zh: 都不用担心：层次聚类会忽略噪声

feedback.en: Hierarchical methods cluster every point; noise ends up in merges.
feedback.zh: 层次方法把每个点都聚进去；噪声会参与合并。

explain.en: Here complete linkage breaks the thin groups, while single can follow them (but beware noise bridges).
explain.zh: 这里全链会拆开细长的组，单链能顺着它们走（但要提防噪声搭桥）。

title.en: Section A: k-means or hierarchical?
title.zh: A 部分：k-means 还是层次聚类？

prompt.en: Compare k-means and agglomerative clustering: name two differences and one limitation of each. (1-3 lines.)
prompt.zh: 比较 k-means 和凝聚层次聚类：各说两处不同，以及各自的一个局限。（1-3 行。）

key_points.en: k-means needs K in advance; agglomerative gives a dendrogram to cut at any level
key_points.zh: k-means 需要预先给 K；凝聚聚类给出可在任意高度切的树状图

key_points.en: k-means partitions and minimises WCSS (locally); hierarchical has no objective and a merge cannot be undone
key_points.zh: k-means 做划分、（局部）最小化 WCSS；层次聚类没有目标函数且合并不可撤销

key_points.en: Limits: k-means is sensitive to initialisation, outliers and non-spherical shapes; linkage choices bring chaining (single) or breaking large clusters (complete)
key_points.zh: 局限：k-means 对初始化、离群点和非球形敏感；链接带来链式效应（单链）或拆大簇（全链）

model_answer.en: k-means needs K and gives a flat partition that minimises WCSS only locally, so it depends on the seeds, outliers and spherical shapes. Agglomerative clustering needs no K (cut the dendrogram), makes no shape assumption beyond the linkage, but has no objective and cannot undo a merge; single linkage chains and complete linkage breaks large clusters.
model_answer.zh: k-means needs K and gives a flat partition that minimises WCSS only locally, so it depends on the seeds, outliers and spherical shapes. Agglomerative clustering needs no K (cut the dendrogram), makes no shape assumption beyond the linkage, but has no objective and cannot undo a merge; single linkage chains and complete linkage breaks large clusters.

explain.en: Two contrasts and a limitation for each is what the marker looks for.
explain.zh: 阅卷看的是两处对比和各自的局限。

title.en: Section C: segmenting customers

prompt.en: A shop has, for 50,000 customers, the number of purchases, mean basket value, and a categorical favourite category. Design a clustering analysis to find customer segments: choose a method, say how you prepare the data, how you choose K, and how you judge the result.
prompt.zh: 一家店有 5 万名顾客的购买次数、平均客单价，以及一个类别型的“最爱品类”。设计一个聚类分析来找顾客群：选方法，说明数据怎么准备，K 怎么选，结果怎么评价。

key_points.en: Scale the numeric features; handle the categorical one (one-hot, or a mixed distance) since the mean is undefined for categories
key_points.zh: 把数值特征缩放；类别型特征要处理（独热编码或混合距离），因为类别没有均值

key_points.en: Method: k-means (large N, scalable); several random seeds, keep the lowest WCSS
key_points.zh: 方法：k-means（N 大，可扩展）；多个随机种子，留 WCSS 最低的

key_points.en: Choose K by elbow and CH index over a range of K; check segments make sense to the business
key_points.zh: 用肘部法和 CH 指数在一个 K 的范围内选 K；检查分群在业务上说得通

key_points.en: Judge: cohesion/separation (WCSS, BCSS, CH), inspect outliers; hierarchical is too costly at this N
key_points.zh: 评价：凝聚度/分离度（WCSS、BCSS、CH），检查离群点；N 这么大，层次聚类开销太高

model_answer.en: Scale the numeric features, one-hot encode the favourite category, and run k-means (scalable to 50,000 customers) with several random seeds, keeping the run with the lowest WCSS. Choose K with the elbow plot and the CH index over, say, K = 2 to 10. Evaluate by cohesion and separation (WCSS, BCSS, CH), look at outliers that distort centroids, and check that the segments are interpretable for the shop. Hierarchical clustering would need an N x N distance matrix, too costly here.
model_answer.zh: Scale the numeric features, one-hot encode the favourite category, and run k-means (scalable to 50,000 customers) with several random seeds, keeping the run with the lowest WCSS. Choose K with the elbow plot and the CH index over, say, K = 2 to 10. Evaluate by cohesion and separation (WCSS, BCSS, CH), look at outliers that distort centroids, and check that the segments are interpretable for the shop. Hierarchical clustering would need an N x N distance matrix, too costly here.

explain.en: A design answer names the method and justifies each choice from the data.
explain.zh: 设计题的答案要给出方法，并从数据出发说明每个选择的理由。

title.en: What to remember

rows.en: no labels; five axes: exclusive/overlapping, hard/soft, hierarchical/partitioning, complete/partial, homogeneous/heterogeneous
rows.zh: 没有标签；五条轴：互斥/重叠、硬/软、层次/划分、完全/部分、同质/异质

rows.en: seed, assign to nearest centroid, update to mean, repeat; normalise first; minimises $J$ = WCSS by coordinate descent, so it always stops, but at a local optimum
rows.zh: 种子，分配到最近质心，更新为均值，重复；先规范化；对 $J$ = WCSS 做坐标下降，所以一定会停，但停在局部最优

rows.en: K given; seeds; outliers; non-spherical; different sizes and densities; no mean for categories
rows.zh: 要给定 K；依赖种子；离群点；非球形；大小和密度不同；类别没有均值

rows.en: elbow in the WCSS curve (never the minimum); CH index
rows.zh: WCSS 曲线的肘部（绝不是最小值）；CH 指数

rows.en: single = min (chains, sensitive to noise, non-elliptical OK); complete = max (compact, breaks large clusters); average = mean; centroid = centres (inversions)
rows.zh: 单链 = 取最小（串链、怕噪声、非椭圆也行）；全链 = 取最大（紧凑、拆大簇）；平均链 = 取平均；质心链 = 比质心（会倒挂）

rows.en: no K needed (cut the dendrogram), no objective, merges cannot be undone
rows.zh: 不需要 K（切树状图），没有目标函数，合并不可撤销

rows.en: $WCSS = \sum_j\sum_{i \in C_j}\lVert x_i - \mu_j\rVert^2$, $BCSS = \sum_j n_j\lVert \mu - \mu_j\rVert^2$, $WCSS + BCSS$ = const; $CH = \frac{BCSS}{WCSS}\cdot\frac{N-K}{K-1}$, higher is better
rows.zh: $WCSS = \sum_j\sum_{i \in C_j}\lVert x_i - \mu_j\rVert^2$，$BCSS = \sum_j n_j\lVert \mu - \mu_j\rVert^2$，$WCSS + BCSS$ 为常数；$CH = \frac{BCSS}{WCSS}\cdot\frac{N-K}{K-1}$，越高越好
